_what: The 29 structure definitions drafted 2026-10-15 and accepted on the structure review sheet (docs/review/structure-2026-10-15.html; accepted with no change). Every quotation checked against the Berean. They move into ontology/kinds.json with vocabulary release 1.2.0.
action: In an action-then-state pair, the first clause: the act as commanded, before it is reported done.
state: In an action-then-state pair, the second clause: the same act reported as having happened.
adv: A participant giving a clause's circumstance (where, when, how, how much) as MACULA marks it: 'And THERE I will provide for you' (Gen 45:11).
agent_act: One clause in a run of acts by one agent, each stating its subject only in its verb, all resolved to the same referent: 'He makes me lie down … He leads me … He restores my soul' (Psa 23:2-3).
aim: A qualifier of a command: what it is for, joined by 'so that': 'Let My people go, so that they may worship Me' (Exod 8:1).
aux: A word a clause carries that is neither a participant nor its predicate: in this graph mostly the Greek interjection or particle that opens it, 'SEE, I lay in Zion a stone' (1 Pet 2:6).
basis: A qualifier of a command: the reason given for it, joined by 'because' or 'for'.
command: The command itself within an Imperative group: one directive clause, or the first of several joined by 'and' ('Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth', Exod 8:16).
conceded: In a concession, the obstacle: the clause introduced by 'even though' that the held claim stands against: 'Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death' (Psa 23:4).
condition: In a conditional, the 'if' clause: the circumstance under which the consequence holds.
consequence: In a conditional, the clause the condition governs. The group takes its force from it, since it is the one that asserts, commands or asks.
described_as: One 'the one who …' clause in a run describing one referent, its unstated subject the run's common one (Psa 103:3-5).
ellipsis: A constituent standing for a clause the text leaves incomplete, its verb understood from context: 'whether good or bad' (2 Cor 5:10).
frame: The clause that frames a communication ('he said', 'he called out') as a member of it: the act of saying, apart from what is said (Gen 45:1).
group_subject: The subject shared by every line of a collection (parallel lines, a run of one agent's acts, or a run of descriptions), held on the group and carried to each line (Psa 119:105).
holds_anyway: In a concession, the claim that holds despite the obstacle: 'I will fear no evil' (Psa 23:4).
io: The participant an act is done to or for, beside its object: 'He forgave US all our trespasses' (Col 2:13).
its_ground: In a concession, why the held claim stands, where the text gives a reason: 'for You are with me' (Psa 23:4).
lest: One clause to the outcome it is meant to prevent, marked by Hebrew פֶּן ('lest', 'or else') (Gen 45:11; 1 Chr 10:4).
line: One line of a parallel pair: the second restates the first's roles without the subject, because the subject is the same.
o: The participant an act is done to: 'Cush was the father of NIMROD' (1 Chr 1:10).
o2: A second object, where a verb takes two: 'she named him PERESH' (1 Chr 7:16).
or: One clause to an alternative to it, joined by 'or'; often two questions side by side (Deut 4:32).
s: The participant a clause's predicate is said of: 'CUSH was the father of Nimrod' (1 Chr 1:10). Where the text leaves it unstated it may be inferred, and the link says how.
tail: A constituent MACULA hangs at the end of a clause, outside its core roles: a trailing phrase, such as the net the disciples came dragging in the Greek of John 21:8.
therefore: One clause to another drawn from it as its consequence, joined by 'therefore' (Hebrew עַל כֵּן, Greek οὖν) (1 Chr 11:7; Col 2:16).
unless: One clause to the exception that would cancel it, joined by 'unless' (Hebrew לוּלֵא).
v: The predicate of a clause: the verb that says what is done or what is.
voice: A writing's authoring voice: a psalm's or a letter's 'I', the role as distinct from the person who fills it (see resolves to).
